role_or_event: Birth (born Annie Elizabeth Lintzenich)
description: Born in Paducah, Kentucky; raised in Indianapolis, Indiana, where she graduated from Cathedral High School.

role_or_event: Bachelor of Science
description: Undergraduate degree; member of Chi Omega sorority. Year of award not stated in the retrieved source.

role_or_event: Doctor of Medicine
description: MD; year of award not stated in the retrieved source.

role_or_event: Pediatrics residency
description: Completed a medical residency in pediatrics in Cincinnati before moving to South Carolina in 2009.

role_or_event: Master of Science in clinical research
description: Master's degree in clinical research, completed after she began work at MUSC Shawn Jenkins Children's Hospital.

role_or_event: Pediatric hospitalist
description: Worked 14 years at the MUSC children's hospital as a pediatric hospitalist; moved to the South Carolina Lowcountry in 2009.

role_or_event: Professor of pediatrics
description: Held a faculty appointment as professor of pediatrics. Start and end dates not stated in the retrieved source.

role_or_event: Joined Moms Demand Action; began clinical research on firearm injury prevention
description: Became politically active after the 2018 Parkland high school shooting, joined the gun-safety group Moms Demand Action, and began clinical research into gun-violence prevention to reduce pediatric firearm injuries.

role_or_event: Announced candidacy, U.S. House, South Carolina's 1st congressional district
description: First run for political office; announced in November 2021.

role_or_event: Won Democratic nomination for U.S. House, SC-01
description: Won the Democratic nomination after running unopposed in the June 2022 primary.

role_or_event: Unpaid leave from MUSC Children's Hospital
description: Announced an unpaid leave while running for Congress, citing threats against doctors and saying she was doing so to protect herself and her colleagues.

role_or_event: Lost general election, U.S. House, SC-01
description: Received 42.5% to incumbent Nancy Mace's 56.5%; conceded by telephone soon afterward.

role_or_event: Founded political action committee 'Their Future. Our Vote'
description: Announced creation of a PAC in April 2023 focused on electing candidates who advocate for children.

role_or_event: Resigned from MUSC
description: Resigned her hospital position in June 2023.

role_or_event: Part-time pediatrician
description: As of mid-2025 worked part-time as a pediatrician at Children's National Hospital while living in Charleston, South Carolina.

role_or_event: Announced candidacy for the U.S. Senate
description: Announced a 2026 Senate campaign aimed at unseating Republican incumbent Lindsey Graham; said she decided to run after Trump appointed Robert F. Kennedy Jr. as Secretary of Health.

role_or_event: Won Democratic nomination for the U.S. Senate
description: Won the Democratic primary on June 9, 2026 and was expected to face Lindsey Graham.

role_or_event: Won general election for the U.S. Senate
description: Defeated Republican nominee Darline Graham, becoming the first woman elected to the U.S. Senate from South Carolina and the first Democrat to win a South Carolina Senate election since 1998.

role_or_event: Assumes office as U.S. Senator
description: Scheduled to assume office on January 3, 2027.

role_or_event: Marriage to Charlie Andrews
description: Married Charlie Andrews, a neurological critical care doctor at MUSC, in 2011; three children; filed for divorce in August 2023, finalized 2024.
